flagged.evidence: The item states that its integrals are nonnegative Lebesgue integrals and later defines G_k using dλ_k. But [F7] is supported by lem-gaussian-integral-is-finite-and-positive, whose title calls it “The improper integral of e^{-x^2} over R,” and [F8] is explicitly a change-of-variable result for improper integrals. These license the improper Riemann value used in step 1.2, not its identification with the Lebesgue value G_1. The usual finite-interval Riemann–Lebesgue equality followed by monotone convergence closes this short gap.
